definition: REST API Design is a core concept in MEAN Stack. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What REST API Design is
theory.body: REST API Design describes the methods and patterns used within MEAN Stack to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: REST API Design is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why REST API Design matters
theory.body: Without REST API Design, systems built with MEAN Stack are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How REST API Design works
theory.body: The mechanism behind REST API Design follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of REST API Design.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of REST API Design
theory.body: REST API Design offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
